# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 18 (Bu-Vb Np18)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np18

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Rūpiya* ("Becoming the owner of money") is the eighteenth *nissaggiya pācittiya* rule in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule establishes that a monk who receives money must relinquish it and confess the offense. The origin story and promulgation of the rule are recorded as taking place at Rājagaha [Entrance to the Vinaya Vol. 3 1983]. A modern English translation of the rule and its commentary is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

The prohibition against accepting money possesses widespread parallels across early Buddhist monastic traditions, appearing in the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga texts of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya schools preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan. It also corresponds to the bhikkhunī lineage (*Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 21) across various recensions, and shares thematic resonance with the *Sattasatikakkhandhaka* (Kd 22) regarding the dispute over money.
